saturation_gate.notes: Corpus exceeds the 100-full-text-PDF threshold (117 verified PDFs), fully resolving institutional Pirivena codes and classical Hindu/Buddhist Tantric guru lineages.

Track A (Burma & Mon Tradition).key_discoveries: Dhammanīti v. 8 & Lokanīti v. 50 contain exact ācariya-chāyā stanza; Pagan inscriptions establish Maṅ chryā / Tape sā spiritual kinship; Ari monks exercised sin-remission power through guru authority; Epigraphia Birmanica (Vols 1-3) & Ray (1936, 1946) document Mon-Burmese guru lineage transmission.

Track B (Sri Lanka & Polonnaruwa Traditi.key_discoveries: Rāmacandra Bhāratī (15th c., King Parākramabāhu VI of Kotte) composed Bhaktiśataka under Sangharāja Śrī Rāhula of Toṭagamuva, blending Hindu bhakti with Buddhist guru devotion; Abhayagiri dhāraṇī stones decode to Amoghavajra tantric tradition (Schopen 1982); Sundberg (2011) documents Vajrabodhi sea transmission; Epigraphia Zeylanica (Vols 2-5) records royal monastic decrees.

Track C (Gurupañcāśikā & Nusantara).key_discoveries: Taishō 1687 (1084 CE) verse T1687, p. 776b14 proves exact parallel: '若足蹈師影 獲罪如毀塔' (treading teacher shadow = destroying stupa); Szántó (2013) & Lévi (1929) verse 15/23 (chāyāṃ na laṅghayed); Brandes & Krom 1913 Inscription CVIII Mantyasih III (907 CE) contains 'gurudrohaka' curse; Acri (2011) Dharma Pātañjala establishes Śaiva-Buddhist ascetic guru transmission.

Track D (Missing Links, Dharmaśāstra & T.key_discoveries: Manusmṛti 2.198-204 & 4.130 (with Kullūka) is the root template for shadow and name prohibitions; P.V. Kane (6 vols) documents guru-śuśrūṣā and prāyaścitta; Lingat (1973) proves Buddhicization into Southeast Asian Thammasat/Dhammathat; Tantric Mūlāpatti #1 is guror avajñānam; Atiśa's 12-year stay in Srivijaya (Chaiya/Sumatra) with Serlingpa shaped Bodhipathapradīpa 62-67; Bizot & Walker document Khmer/Thai guru-treading curses.

Track E (Classical Hindu Tantric Traditi.key_discoveries: Kularṇava Tantra Ullāsas 11-13 (Vidyaratna/Avalon 1917 & Pandit 1965) establish comprehensive theology of Guru-sevā, Gurupādukā, Gurumantra, and horrific retributions for Gurunindā/Gurudroha (vv. 12.12, 12.32, 12.41, 13.9, 13.15, 13.24-27); Śāradātilaka Tantra Paṭala 2 (Avalon 1933) establishes 1-year mutual testing period & rigorous qualifications of guru and śiṣya (Padārthādarśa); Tantrarāja Tantra (1918, 1926) establishes Tripurasundarī identification; Mālinīvijayottaratantra (KSTS 37, 1922) codifies Śaiva śaktipāta; Kaulajñānanirṇaya (Bagchi 1934) establishes Matsyendranātha's yoginīkaula guru transmission; Sanderson (2001, 2009) frames Saiva royal guru dominance.

Track F (Early Buddhist Tantric Manuals.key_discoveries: Kriyāsaṃgraha of Kuladatta (Rani 1977 & Tanemura 1993) codifies vajrācārya's supreme authority over 4 nikāyas in ritual construction and abhiṣeka; Vajrāvalī of Abhayākaragupta (Rani 1977, Hemis Tibetan MS 1983, Mori 1992) synthesizes 26 mandalas with disciple submission, surrender of body/wealth, and samayodaka (pledge-water) oath; Advayavajrasaṃgraha (Shastri 1927 GOS 40) explicitly codifies Caturdaśa-mūlāpatti #1 as vajrācāryasya paribhavanam with direct fall to Avīci mahāghora naraka; Sādhanamālā, Two Vajrayāna Works, Guhyasamāja Tantra (GOS 53).

Track G (Sri Lankan Piriveṇas, Katikāvat.key_discoveries: Totagamuwa Vijayabāhu Piriveṇa (Śrī Rāhula) & Padmāvatī Piriveṇa (Vanaratana) operated as international monastic universities teaching Sanskrit, Veda, Chhandas, and Alankāra (Ranaweera 2025); Polonnaruwa Katikāvata (1165 CE, Gal-vihāra) & Dambadeniya Katikāvata (1266 CE) institutionalized strict examination of disciples (jātigotra vicārā), 4 classes of antevāsika, and absolute preceptor authority; Vṛttamālākhyā (1894) and Vyāsakāra Śatakam (1880) functioned as curricular guru-eulogies.

Track H (Pan-Asian Epigraphy & Reference.key_discoveries: Epigraphia Indica (Vols 1-8) and Sircar (1965, 1971) establish epigraphic foundations of monastic land grants, teacher-pupil designations (ācariya-antevāsin), and pan-Asian imprecatory curse formulas (śāpa/gurudroha).

Track I (User Contributed Primary Texts.key_discoveries: Epigraphia Zeylanica Vol. 1 (Wickremasinghe 1912) and Vol. 3 (1933) fully retrieved; Vol. 2 upgraded to full OCR-searchable layer (Polonnaruwa Katikāvata); Upāsakajanālaṅkāra complete Pāli text (2,532 lines) integrated; Jolly (1881) Dharmasūtra review; Berkwitz (2019) relic/image authority narratives; Kaloyanides (2021) Hallisey regional ethics.
